claims.statement: `create_deep_agent` assembles a LangGraph agent from caller tools, a selected backend, ordered Deep Agents middleware, and optional checkpointer, store, cache, context, and state schemas; the resulting graph is configured with recursion limit 9,999 and Deep Agents integration/version metadata.

The main middleware assembly puts filesystem and synchronous-subagent support before summarization and dangling-tool-call repair, optionally adds async subagents, inserts caller middleware ahead of the profile/skills/caching/memory tail, and applies tool exclusion after custom middleware so excluded tools cannot be restored by a custom wrapper.

`FilesystemMiddleware` enforces declared filesystem rules at its built-in tools rather than direct backend access: first matching rules allow, deny, or interrupt calls, and `create_deep_agent` converts interrupt-mode rules into filesystem `interrupt_on` entries before merging caller entries, with caller entries taking precedence for duplicate tool names.

`DeepAgentState.messages` uses a `DeltaChannel` with the local message reducer and snapshot frequency 50, reducing message checkpoint growth from O(N²) to O(N); graph construction passes an optional caller checkpointer through to LangChain rather than supplying a persistence implementation itself.

The message delta reducer coerces raw message-like inputs, deduplicates/replaces messages by stable ID, applies removals and last `REMOVE_ALL_MESSAGES` reset semantics, and treats `None` replay state as empty; stable IDs are intentionally assigned before checkpoint serialization rather than during replay.

Deep Agents collects `PrivateStateAttr` fields from caller and middleware state schemas and installs them on task middleware; normal inline delegation strips these keys both before child invocation and before merging child results, while unresolvable runtime annotations are warned about and cannot be protected.

`PatchToolCallsMiddleware` repairs a resumed history containing AI tool calls without matching results by appending error `ToolMessage` records and replacing the message state with a `REMOVE_ALL_MESSAGES` reset followed by the repaired history.

Top-level and declarative-subagent effective filesystem or explicit tool interrupt configuration installs `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware`; declarative subagents inherit parent `permissions` and `interrupt_on` unless they provide their own configuration, whereas compiled and remote async subagents own approval configuration in their separate graphs.

The synchronous `task` tool invokes selected inline subagents and returns a tool-call-correlated `ToolMessage`, serializing a structured response when present or otherwise selecting the last non-empty AI text; compiled subagents must return state containing `messages` or the task call fails.

Declarative subagents can be isolated or experimental forks: isolated children receive the delegated task as a new human message, while forks inherit selected parent state and conversation, cannot define their own skills, and reject recursive delegation; compiled subagents do not inherit the parent custom state schema.

Remote async subagents run through the LangGraph SDK against Agent Protocol servers, return task IDs immediately, and persist local task status in the `async_tasks` state field whose reducer merges updates by task ID; local ASGI transport without a URL requires async parent invocation.
Binary base64 message payloads are offloaded best-effort to backend paths under `{artifacts_root}/blobs/<sha256>` and replaced with `deepagents_blob` digest references; failed uploads remain inline.

Blob hydration reuses cached payloads or downloads referenced digests, verifies downloaded bytes against the SHA-256 reference, and replaces unavailable or invalid blobs with a text notice rather than restoring unverified content.

Async task management preserves a remote task's identity while operating it: checks update stored status and return successful output, updates interrupt the current remote run and create a replacement run on the same thread, cancellation records `cancelled`, and list uses live status for nonterminal tasks with cached-status fallback on lookup failure.

An async fork serializes a snapshot of the parent effective conversation after clearing local tool artifacts and eviction metadata, hydrates portable blob content before dispatch, and sends it to a remote graph whose prompt, tools, and other runtime resources remain independent.

Filesystem-derived approval is path-sensitive: exact tools test a validated requested path and, when available, its symlink-resolved target, while bulk tools pause when their search or delete subtree overlaps an interrupt-rule anchor; missing bulk paths, current-directory aliases, absolute `glob` patterns, and relative patterns containing `..` are handled conservatively to prevent HITL bypass.

Generated filesystem approval entries are limited to tools whose read or write operation has an interrupt rule and allow `approve`, `edit`, `reject`, and `respond`; an exact-path deny decision suppresses an interrupt, and approved calls still enter filesystem denial enforcement.

A nonempty filesystem permission set is rejected for an execution-capable backend because `execute` has no tool-level permission policy, except when every rule is scoped to a configured `CompositeBackend` route.
